newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF to allow multi-service accounts for brokerages from Oct. [CORRECTED 09:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: MOF to allow multi-service accounts for brokerages from Oct. [CORRECTED 09:35 GMT]

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Thursday it will allow brokerages to set up multi-service accounts for clients from October 1. (Corrects type of account from "wrap" to "multi-service".)
The move is part of Japan's overall "Big Bang" financial reforms mapped out by the government in June.

Multi-service accounts will enable customers to purchase stocks and pay public utilities bills through accounts they had set up mainly for short-term securities investment trust funds, a MOF statement said.
It also said that investment trust management firms will be allowed to sell securities investment trusts over-the-counter at banks from December 1.
Rules on cancellations and payments for money market funds and medium-term government bond funds will be abolished from August 1, the statement said.
It added that banks' securities units will be allowed to engage in trading of convertible bonds, warrants and warrant bonds in the secondary market from October 1.
The banks' units will also be allowed to enter into stock index futures and options trading, so long as it does not involve the delivery of stocks.

Brokerages' trust bank subsidiaries will be allowed to manage all types of cash trust funds from October 1, excluding pension trust funds and most types of joint operating designated money trusts, the statement said. (c) Reuters Limited 1997
